issue_body: This build adds a helper Math.formatBytes(n: number): string that formats a byte count human-readably using 1024-based units. The rule it should follow: pick the largest unit (B, KB, MB, GB) whose 1024-power fits in the value, divide the value by that 1024-power, and print the result with the unit. Bytes have no decimal places; KB/MB/GB are rounded to one decimal place, so e.g. 512 -> "512 B", 1536 -> "1.5 KB", 1610612736 -> "1.5 GB". Something is wrong at the unit boundaries: 1024 prints as "1024 B" instead of "1 KB", and 1048576 prints in KB instead of "1 MB". Figure out what is going on and fix it so formatBytes picks the right unit.
